record.original_question: Let α_i and λ_i be null sequences with α_i → 0 and λ_i → 0, and for each i let K_i be the middle-α_i Cantor set whose first construction interval is [0, λ_i]. If S is the associated sumset, is it generically true that the Hausdorff dimension satisfies dim_H(S) = ∑_{i=1}^∞ dim_H(K_i)? If not, in which specific cases does this equality hold?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
For each positive integer $i$, let $\alpha_i \in (0,1)$ and $\lambda_i > 0$, and assume that both sequences $(\alpha_i)$ and $(\lambda_i)$ tend to $0$ as $i \to \infty$. For each $i$, let $K_i \subset \mathbb{R}$ be the middle-$\alpha_i$ Cantor set built on the initial interval $[0, \lambda_i]$; that is, $K_i$ is obtained by the standard iterated removal of the open middle subinterval of relative length $\alpha_i$ from each surviving closed interval, starting from $[0,\lambda_i]$. Define the sumset
$$S = \Bigl\{\sum_{i=1}^{\infty} x_i : x_i \in K_i \text{ for every } i\Bigr\},$$
which is well defined as a compact subset of $\mathbb{R}$ under suitable summability of the $\lambda_i$. Let $\dim_H$ denote Hausdorff dimension.

(a) Determine whether, in a generic sense (e.g.\ for typical choices of the parameter sequences $(\alpha_i)$ and $(\lambda_i)$), one has the identity
$$\dim_H(S) \;=\; \sum_{i=1}^{\infty} \dim_H(K_i).$$

(b) If this equality does not hold generically, characterize the specific classes of sequences $(\alpha_i)$ and $(\lambda_i)$ for which the equality holds.
artifact.status_search_result: A web search located related work on subsums of null sequences, signed null sequences and Hausdorff dimension, and on sums of homogeneous/middle Cantor sets, but none of the located references explicitly resolves whether the Hausdorff dimension of the infinite sumset $S$ equals $\sum_i \dim_H(K_i)$ generically, nor gives a complete characterization of equality cases. The status thus appears unverified from public sources.

status_evidence.title: Signed null sequences and Hausdorff dimension
status_evidence.snippet: Studies Hausdorff dimension of sets of sign sequences making a null sequence sum convergent; does not address dim_H(S) = sum dim_H(K_i).
status_evidence.claim: Related but does not resolve the asked dimension identity for middle-alpha Cantor sumsets.

status_evidence.title: On the sum of two homogeneous Cantor sets
status_evidence.snippet: Recent work on sums of homogeneous Cantor sets, providing dimension/measure conditions for finite sums.
status_evidence.claim: Treats finite sums of Cantor sets, not the infinite sumset of middle-alpha Cantor sets considered here.
